en.title: Hawaii Island rescue helicopter 'Ka'Io': Sayre foundation equips first responders with an Airbus H125
en.summary: An Airbus story describes how the Daniel R. Sayre Memorial Foundation equipped Hawaii Island first responders with an Airbus H125 helicopter, named Ka'Io, so mountain and remote rescues no longer depend on carrying patients down on stretchers.
body: In 1997, Daniel R. Sayre died while hiking to Kapaloa Falls in Pololu Valley, and his parents created a memorial foundation honouring the first responders who spent 10 hours recovering his body. Over more than 28 years, the foundation has raised money in the community for the Hawaii Fire Department, buying gear, trucks, vessels and training. The department handles search and rescue, emergency medical service, fire suppression and lifeguarding across Hawaii Island, which covers 4,000 square miles and is home to 200,000 residents.

After a wildfire threatened the home of one of the island's benefactors, the foundation helped fund its first H125 helicopter, designated Ka'Io, or 'The hawk'. The H125 was chosen for its ability to ascend Mauna Loa and Mauna Kea, each just under 14,000 feet, terrain that draws climbers and skiers; previously, rescuers had to load injured people onto stretchers and hike them down. The story also recounts a man in the south who lost his leg below the knee in a mower accident: Ka'Io reached him in 25 minutes, compared with an hour and a half by ambulance, and flew him to hospital, saving his life.

facts.claim: Daniel R. Sayre died in 1997 while hiking to Kapaloa Falls in Pololu Valley, and his parents created a memorial foundation honouring the first responders who worked 10 hours to recover his body.
The Daniel R. Sayre Memorial Foundation funded the first H125 helicopter, designated Ka'Io, or 'The hawk', after a wildfire threatened the home of one of the island's benefactors.
The H125 was chosen for its ability to ascend Mauna Loa and Mauna Kea, each just under 14,000 feet, where rescuers previously had to carry injured people down on stretchers.

In a mower accident in the south of the island, Ka'Io reached a man who had lost his leg below the knee in 25 minutes, while an ambulance would have taken an hour and a half, and flew him to hospital.

zh.title: 夏威夷大島救護直升機「Ka'Io」：塞爾紀念基金會為第一線添購空中巴士H125
zh.summary: 空中巴士專文介紹，丹尼爾·塞爾紀念基金會如何為夏威夷大島第一線救護人員添購空中巴士H125直升機「Ka'Io」，讓山區與偏遠地區的救援不再只能靠人力抬運下山。
body: 1997年，丹尼爾·塞爾在前往波洛盧谷卡帕洛阿瀑布健行途中喪生；他的父母隨後成立紀念基金會，向當年花了10小時尋回丹尼爾遺體的第一線救護人員致敬。基金會成立28年多來持續為夏威夷大島消防局募款，補齊裝備、車輛、船隻與訓練；夏威夷大島面積4,000平方英里、居民20萬人，消防局同時負責搜救、緊急醫療、滅火與救生工作。

在一場野火威脅島上一名捐助者住家之後，基金會與相關單位展開合作，資助添購第一架H125直升機，並命名為「Ka'Io」，意為「老鷹」。H125獲選的原因是它能飛抵將近14,000英尺高的冒納羅亞火山與冒納凱亞火山山頂；過去事故發生時，救護人員只能把傷者放在擔架上徒步抬下山，如今直升機能飛往島上任何一座山的山頂。文中還提到一名南部男子在割草機事故中膝下截肢，救護直升機25分鐘就抵達，遠快於救護車所需的1個半小時，並把他送醫保住性命。
